rev.why: All values checked against Tables 3-4 (pp. 7-8) and the text (pp. 7-12): correct. But the verdicts are phrased as effects of a component against the baseline (e.g. 'planning works'), not as a quality and cost verdict for each configuration on its own as §6 asks; the author should decide whether to restate them per configuration

Values were right, but the verdicts were effects of a component against its baseline ('planning works') and several configurations (T0, T1-T3, the T4/128k baselines) had none; §6 and draft-verify require each configuration, baseline included, to be judged on its own. Verdicts redone from each configuration's own values (Tables 3-4, pp. 7-8, rebuilt from the pdftotext column dump by row order and checked against the text deltas p. 9-12); ranges over 32k-128k computed here. Thresholds are the extractor's (paper sets none), as in other r2 drafts: quality does not work below about 20% success, partly when it resolves part but not nearly all tasks; cost works up to about $1.5 per task
Rule 1: extractor-chosen thresholds removed and verdicts replaced with "no criterion stated by the authors" (the authors set no success threshold); configurations and metric values kept.

fields.v: Benchmarks: SWE-Bench Verified (500), Terminal-Bench 2.1 (89). Configurations: T0-T4 x 32k/64k/96k/128k (planning on, predefined tools), plus planning-off and bash-only at T4/128k; 4 models (Nemotron-3 30B/120B/550B, Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B). Baselines: T0 for context management; T4/128k with planning and tools for the other ablations. Held constant: execution loop, safety gates, post-edit diagnostics, stuck detection, model serving (SGLang BF16, T 0, top-p 0.95, 16,384 output tokens), 300-step cap, thresholds. Acceptance: benchmark verifiers. Repetitions: 1 run per task and setting. Human intervention: none. Tests: two-sided exact McNemar with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR 0.05 per comparison family

Context management helps most under tight budgets, mainly by preventing overflow (T0 overflow 78.7% -> 8.7% SWE, 61.0% -> 12.1% Terminal from 32k to 128k; managed tiers 0%). T4 comparable success with lowest mean cost at every budget. Recall rarely used (36 of 64 T2/T4 settings never call it). Planning: +11.6 pts SWE and +4.5 Terminal for 30B at higher cost (+75% on Terminal); for 550B and Mistral cost -30% / -32% on SWE with -2.0 / -0.4 pts. Bash-only: 550B +3.6 / +5.6 pts with -53% / -30% cost; Mistral -23.2 pts on SWE but +6.7 on Terminal; 30B collapses (66% of Terminal bash-only runs end on out-of-interface calls). Many differences marked significant (asterisks in Tables 3-4); many Terminal-Bench contrasts not significant

Distinguished components and showed model- and budget-dependent effects; trajectory analysis explains mechanisms. Repeatability: single run per task, temperature 0. Limitations stated: one implementation of each component (planning prompt, threshold policy); action-space intervention bundles tool availability, prompts, state tracking and diagnostics; planning and action space ablated only at T4/128k (no full factorial); single run per task, Terminal-Bench only 89 tasks (low power); two model families, SWE-Bench Python-only; model size imperfect proxy for capability

Harness design is a conditional systems problem: select components for the target model, task type and budget rather than by default. Crossover points need validation on other model families, harnesses and task types; full factorial study needed

Not about SDD. Tables 3-4 columns jumbled by pdftotext; 128k and ablation rows rebuilt and checked against text deltas (e.g. 30B planning +11.6, 550B bash cost -53%, Mistral tools +23.2). Asterisks (significance) kept only where visible. Code or data release not stated (no repository URL found). Prompts, tool descriptions and judge prompts in App. A-C. Costs are OpenRouter list prices applied to locally served models. No pre-registration. Language: Python (SWE-Bench) and shell
